title: Geometry versus excitation sector in the decoherence of asymmetric $N$-qubit $W$ states
authors: Sougata Bhattacharyya, Sovik Roy, Fatih Ozaydin
abstract: We investigate how network geometry and excitation sector separately control pairwise entanglement decay in asymmetric multipartite $W$ states. To disentangle these effects, we introduce an analytically tractable $N$-qubit generalization of the asymmetric Lohmayer geometry and its complementary-excitation partner, yielding inequivalent vertex-base (VB) and base-base (BB) pair classes that can be compared directly with symmetric $W$-state references. We derive closed-form concurrence dynamics under representative one-sided noise models and find that, within either excitation sector, the VB concurrence has exactly the same noise dependence as the corresponding symmetric reference, preserving a noise-independent proportional advantage wherever both remain entangled. The amplitude-damping reordering previously identified for the three-qubit Lohmayer state is therefore a cross-sector effect rather than an intrinsic fragility of the VB geometry. In contrast, the BB pair exhibits a genuine same-sector structural fragility, with lower entanglement-sudden-death thresholds than the VB pair under depolarizing noise and, in the $(N-1)$-excitation sector, under amplitude damping. The results establish network geometry, excitation sector, and noise symmetry as distinct ingredients governing pairwise entanglement robustness in asymmetric quantum networks.
summary: This paper analyzes the decoherence of asymmetric N-qubit W states by separating the effects of network geometry from the excitation sector. Using closed-form concurrence dynamics under various noise models, the authors show that different pair classes exhibit distinct vulnerabilities to noise. The work establishes that entanglement robustness is governed by three independent factors: geometry, excitation sector, and noise symmetry.
main_problem: The study investigates how network geometry and excitation sector independently govern the decay of pairwise entanglement within asymmetric N-qubit W states.
main_result: The analysis distinguishes between structural fragility (seen in Base-Base pairs) and cross-sector effects, establishing that geometry, sector, and noise symmetry are distinct controls on entanglement robustness.
method: The authors derived closed-form concurrence dynamics for generalized asymmetric W states under various one-sided local quantum noise models.

key_observables: Pairwise entanglement decay, measured by concurrence; comparison between Vertex-Base (VB) and Base-Base (BB) pair classes.
important_parameters: Noise types include Phase Damping (PD), Amplitude Damping (AD), Depolarization (DP), and Generalized Amplitude Damping (GAD). The system size N is a key parameter.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on a one-sided local-noise convention, where the noise channel acts only on one qubit in any bipartite subsystem.
figures_summary: Figures compare AD concurrence decay for symmetric vs. asymmetric states and illustrate how ESD thresholds depend on N under different noise models.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares decoherence dynamics of symmetric versus asymmetric W states by separating network geometry from the excitation sector, deriving closed-form concurrences for various pair classes.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous theoretical framework to decouple structural properties (geometry vs. excitation) governing entanglement decay in complex quantum networks, which is crucial for designing robust quantum communication protocols.
